source.section: 第五篇 辅助检查 第一章 心电图 第六节

textbook_summary: P waves are replaced by continuous, regular sawtooth F waves without an isoelectric baseline, clearly visible in II, III and aVF.
The atrial rate is 240-350/min, commonly with fixed 2:1 or 4:1 conduction; QRS complexes are usually narrow.
scope: A single regular flutter example. Electrode amplitudes, F-wave contour and timing are authored choices, not anatomical localization. F waves continuously overlap QRS/T.
limitations: Fixed 300/min with 2:1, 3:1 or 4:1 conduction; no variable-conduction or impure-flutter patterns.
Flutter mechanical contraction is not modeled; normal AtrialMechanical events and the normal CVP a wave are suppressed.
The 2:1 physiology demo shortens pulse/pressure morphology support to 320 ms while retaining existing ejection and RC parameters; these are not calibrated hemodynamics.
QT is fixed at 300 ms, without beatwise QT feedback or clinical detection.
The 3:1 example has a ventricular rate of 100/min and retains the 160 ms mechanical offset, 80 ms QRS, 300 ms QT and continuous F waves. These do not establish calibrated flutter filling or ejection.

summary: Primary case report explicitly records3:1 flutter; supports ratio availability, not this authored300/min timing or electrode amplitudes.
